willkommen.3: And we'd be over the moon if you came to celebrate this unforgettable day with us on the Croatian coast.
willkommen.4: A trip to Croatia isn't something you do on a whim – which makes us all the more grateful to every single one of you who makes the journey. To keep your trip as relaxed as possible, we've gathered all the important info on accommodation, travel and the schedule right here on this website.
willkommen.5: Let us know by 1 May 2027 whether you can make it (RSVP).
willkommen.6: We can't wait to raise a glass with you and make memories that last a lifetime!
story.3: That's the honourable name for the union of two hearts: King Ivan and his Queen Nghi – lovingly coined by the family.
story.4: A one-of-a-kind blend of Croatian and Vietnamese roots, strictly certified “Made in Germany”.
story.5: It's the beautiful proof that even a simple swipe to the right can be part of God's divine plan – one that guided two hearts through a sea of possibilities to find their eternal kingdom, built on faith, love and togetherness.
story.8: In case some of you are wondering why it says NGHIVAN all over this website, even though you might know me as Minnie or Minh Nghi – here's the quick explanation for everyone who isn't familiar with how Vietnamese names work:
story.9: In Vietnamese, the name you actually go by comes right at the end. Nghi is my real first name and Minh is my middle name. Combine Minh Nghi with a bunch of kindergartners who couldn't pronounce it, and voilà – my nickname Minnie was born!
story.11: It looks like a little tongue twister at first, but it's actually easy: just think of the word “singer”, swap the “er” for an “ee” – then drop the beginning and only say the back part:
story.17: Depends on who you ask! We told our parents we bumped into each other on a night out (which is true!).
story.18: What we left out: a little swipe to the right is what got the ball rolling. On our first evening together, a digital match turned into a real match for life.
story.19: What happens when one of us gets hungry?
story.21: While Ivan handles hunger pretty well, Nghi without food turns into a genuine force of nature.
story.22: Ivan's survival hack: Always carry an emergency snack or know where the next one is. One little bite – and peace in the relationship is restored!
story.23: Who takes longer in the morning, and who's to blame for being late?
story.24: The official story: Ivan stubbornly insists in front of everyone – and everyone dutifully believes him – that it's always Nghi's fault, of course.
story.25: The truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth: It's Ivan. EVERY. SINGLE. TIME!
story.26: While Nghi is standing at the door, fully ready with shoes and jacket on, Ivan suddenly remembers he urgently needs to go number two. And boom: once again it looks to the outside world like Nghi was the one dawdling. Nice save, Ivan!
story.28: Did Nghi see the proposal coming?
story.30: Not really! After the Vietnam holiday – where Nghi was fully expecting a proposal and nothing happened – expectations for the spontaneous trip to Greece were at rock bottom. The only precaution: the nails still got done before the flight, of course (“You never know…”). 💅
story.32: Ivan's plan was set for the weekend. On his frantic hunt for the “perfect spot”, he kept pestering Nghi with weird questions, didn't listen to the answers and drove her up the wall. On Sunday evening, things blew up big time. It was so strange that Nghi was afraid this would be the holiday where they realise they're just not right for each other!
story.34: After a romantic dinner, Ivan finally popped the question on their evening stroll. Nghi cried such loud happy tears that she missed half of Ivan's speech. Ivan even had to double-check whether Nghi had actually said “YES!” …
story.35: What does it mean to us that you'll be at our wedding?
story.37: We don't take it for granted for a second that you're making the time, taking on the trip to Croatia and putting in the money & effort to celebrate this special day with us. It means so incredibly much to us.
story.38: At the same time, we completely understand if you can't make the journey – you'll still be with us in our hearts! To everyone raising a glass with us: we can't wait to make unforgettable memories together. We love you all! ❤️
unterkunft.2: So you don't have to walk far after the party, we've put together your options for places to stay around our wedding venue in Petrčane. Whether it's full hotel comfort with a sea view or a cosy apartment or villa with friends & family – just pick whatever suits your plans and budget best!
unterkunft.4: If you'd like to stay at the hotel, you can enter our discount code for 5 % directly on hotel-pinija.hr (sadly that's all we could get 😭).
unterkunft.11: For everyone who likes maximum comfort: you can stay right on site at the 4-star Hotel Pinija. After the party you'll practically stumble straight from the dance floor into bed – and enjoy breakfast with a sea view the next morning.
unterkunft.18: Holiday rentals & Airbnbs <small>Right next door & cheaper</small>
unterkunft.19: Petrčane has gorgeous private apartments, guesthouses and villas with pools. Many of them are right behind Hotel Pinija (just a 2 to 5 minute walk). Usually much cheaper and perfect for families or groups of friends.
unterkunft.21: How to find them: Just search for “Petrčane” on Airbnb or Booking.com.
unterkunft.22: 💡 Team up? Want to share a holiday apartment or villa with other guests but don't know who else is looking? Just ask us – we'd love to connect you!
unterkunft.23: 🌊 Important beach info: In Croatia, all beaches are open to the public! Even if you're not staying at the hotel, you're free to use the beach at Hotel Pinija. Just bring your own towels or beach mats (the hotel's fixed sun loungers cost extra or are reserved for hotel guests).
unterkunft.28: Outside Petrčane <small>Nearby villages & the Zadar area</small>
unterkunft.29: If you don't want to spend your whole stay in Petrčane, the surrounding coastal towns are a great base too. A popular combo: 1–2 nights close to the action and the rest of your trip in a cosy holiday rental or at a campsite in the quieter villages nearby.
unterkunft.30: Why the nearby villages are ideal for a beach holiday: Zadar's city centre has a historic old town and great restaurants, but the city beaches usually aren't as beautiful as the ones in the surrounding villages.
unterkunft.31: Our tip: Enjoy the crystal-clear sea in the villages during the day, and only head into Zadar in the evening for strolling, culture and dinner. You'll find more tips under Travel.
unterkunft.34: If you want to stay together as a group, have more independence or extend your stay: here are our favourite places nearby – just book directly on the platform of your choice.
travel.flug.1: <small class="h3__pre">Nearest airport:</small> Zadar International Airport <small>(ZAD) · 20 min to Hotel Pinija</small>
travel.flug.2: For our guests from the Munich / Bavaria area: we've flown to Zadar from Memmingen Airport (FMM) lots of times.
travel.flug.5: Midweek flights can be ridiculously cheap – with a bit of luck and only a small backpack/carry-on, you can get tickets from as little as 35 € per flight.
travel.flug.8: There are cheap off-site car parks (about a 10–15 minute walk from the terminal) where 4–5 days only cost around 40 €.
travel.flug.9: Allow buffer time at the barrier
travel.flug.10: You may have to wait a bit for spaces to free up. Our trick: time your arrival at the car park to 1–2 incoming flights before yours – that way you catch exactly the moment when returning passengers drive out.
travel.us.1: For our guests traveling from the US
travel.us.2: Great news for everyone flying in from the States: United Airlines offers a direct nonstop flight from Newark directly to Split!
travel.us.6: Getting from Split to Petrčane / Zadar
travel.us.7: Split Airport is about a 1.5-hour scenic drive along the coast up to Petrčane. Renting a car directly at Split Airport is super easy and the best way to travel to the wedding location while having total flexibility to explore the coastline!
travel.us.9: Alternatively, look for convenient 1-stop connections directly into Zadar Airport (ZAD), which is just 20 minutes from Hotel Pinija.
travel.auto.7: ⛽ Fuel tip: Make sure you fill up first in Austria and then again in Croatia – fuel there is usually much cheaper.
travel.auto.9: Please, please remember to buy your toll passes online before you leave! It saves loads of time at the toll booths and avoids expensive fines.
travel.auto.12: Section tolls: Tunnel fees on the Tauern motorway (Tauern and Katschberg tunnels) and for the Karawanken tunnel heading south.
travel.auto.14: E-Vinjeta: Digital vignette for the Slovenian motorway network (1-week or 1-month, depending on how long you're staying).
travel.auto.15: Officially in advance from ASFINAG →
travel.auto.17: Just grab a ticket when you get on the motorway and pay when you get off (cash or conveniently by credit card).
travel.auto.18: ⚠️ Important for the drive home (Karawanken tunnel)
travel.auto.19: If you drive north through the Karawanken tunnel on your way home, the northbound tunnel toll is paid directly on the Slovenian side at the Hrušica toll station – not in advance via the Austrian ASFINAG.
travel.auto.22: We've driven this route countless times and always make these two stops:
travel.auto.24: Start – about 9 hours to the coast.
travel.auto.26: Perfect for cheap fuel. Right next to the JET petrol station there's a McDonald's for a quick snack. You have to leave the motorway briefly, but the detour is worth it!
travel.auto.28: Petrol station – from here we take the country roads. Heads up, it's very winding – if you get carsick easily, pack some travel sickness tablets!
travel.auto.30: If you'd rather wait to fill up in Croatia, you can stop right after the border at the INA petrol station (warning: LOTS of mosquitoes!). Fuel at the motorway stations is definitely more expensive.
travel.auto.32: You made it – straight into the sea! 🌊
anreise.3: We strongly recommend booking a rental car. Public transport isn't really used much locally and is hard to judge (we've honestly never used it there ourselves). With a rental car you're super flexible and can get anywhere with ease!
anreise.6: To make your holiday on the Croatian coast perfect, here are our most important insider tips.
anreise.8: A must for first-timers! They protect your feet from sharp pebbles and sea urchins. There are also nice-looking ones that look like (white) sneakers. We got ours on Amazon.
anreise.10: Thin foldable foam mats or padded beach mats make lying on pebbles really comfy – a towel usually isn't enough.
anreise.12: Thanks to the pebble beaches, the water is crystal clear – you can see the underwater world perfectly!
anreise.14: Perfect for swimmers, e.g. to the Kornati islands or Dugi Otok. The boat stops in dreamy bays so you can swim and snorkel right off the deck. We've only been on one so far and can really recommend it. Get in touch with us for links (swimmers only).
anreise.16: Even though Croatia uses the euro and cards work almost everywhere, small beach bars, bakeries or parking meters sometimes only take cash.
anreise.18: The sun is intense – and in the evenings under the pine trees, mosquito spray is your friend.
anreise.21: Zadar · Nin · Ražanac · Posedarje · Novigrad · Sukošan
anreise.23: Dugi Otok – highly recommended: book a guided boat tour!
anreise.25: Vodice · Šibenik · Split · Makarska · Gradac · Drvenik (Brin)
anreise.29: 🎬 Game of Thrones filming locations Dubrovnik (King’s Landing) and Split (Daenerys’ dragon dungeon) are right on the coast.
anreise.30: 🏝️ Islands & boat trips Book a day cruise or, if you have a boating licence, rent a boat yourself.
anreise.31: 🍷 Wine & olive oil Laid-back tastings in traditional konobas in the hinterland.
anreise.32: 🏛️ Culture & evenings Old-town strolls, restaurants and bars in Zadar (15 min) or Split.
anreise.33: Krka National Park Spectacular waterfalls and wooden boardwalks near Šibenik.
anreise.34: Trogir Historic UNESCO old town on a small island just before Split.
anreise.35: Primošten Picturesque fishing village on a peninsula with a lovely promenade.
anreise.36: Omiš Where the river meets the sea – steep cliffs, ziplining & rafting.
anreise.37: Hvar & Brač E.g. Bol / Golden Horn – by ferry from Split.
anreise.38: Ston & Mali Ston Europe's longest fortress wall & fresh oysters.
anreise.39: Kravica Waterfalls On the way to Mostar (BiH) – perfect for a swim.

meta.title: Minh Nghi & Ivan · 4 September 2027
meta.description: We're getting married! Minh Nghi & Ivan – Saturday, 4 September 2027 in Petrčane, Croatia. All the info on accommodation, travel and RSVP.
area.1.character: Petrčane's quiet neighbouring village, surrounded by lots of greenery. A very exclusive and laid-back coastal spot (rumour has it Luka Modrić has a house here too).
area.1.perfect: Holidaymakers looking for quiet, private accommodation who still want to be in Petrčane or Zadar in no time.
area.2.character: A green, exclusive peninsula right next to Petrčane. Upscale resorts, beautiful well-kept stretches of beach and a gorgeously lit coastal promenade.
area.2.perfect: Anyone who likes things a little quieter, close to nature and chic, but still wants to be right near the action.
area.3.sub: The home village in the hinterland
area.3.character: A tiny, charming mountain village where Ivan's family has its roots and where his parents live. Green hills and imposing mountains instead of sea views – and yet only minutes from the quieter beaches on the coast.
area.3.perfect: Anyone who wants to experience authentic, rural Croatia far away from mass tourism (perfect with a rental car).
area.4.character: An authentic, slightly more rugged coastal town on the Velebit Channel with wonderfully clear water and beautiful natural beaches. Life here is still very unspoilt and relaxed.
area.4.perfect: Peace-seekers, nature lovers and anyone who wants to escape the hustle and bustle. Spectacular views of the Velebit mountains!
area.5.character: A lively but relaxed coastal town with the huge Marina Dalmacija and child-friendly pebble and sand beaches. Lots of Ivan's lads will be staying here too (after the wedding)!
area.5.perfect: Anyone looking for a sociable vibe. There's no big party strip, but there are nice beach bars and restaurants.
area.6.character: The historic port city and cultural heart of the region: Roman ruins, Venetian city walls, the Sea Organ and the “Greeting to the Sun” light installation.
area.6.perfect: Anyone looking for city life, sightseeing, a huge choice of accommodation and a proper nightlife scene.
area.7.character: The heart of the wedding! A charming old fishing village with shady pine forests right by the pebble and rock beach, cosy taverns and fantastic sea views.
area.7.perfect: All guests who just want to fall into bed after the party without having to drive anywhere.
area.8.character: Croatia's oldest royal town, idyllically set on a small island in a shallow lagoon. Famous for the kilometre-long Queen's Beach and its healing mud baths.
area.8.perfect: Families with kids, sandy-beach lovers and history buffs. Hardly any nightlife – but real holiday vibes instead.
